dimensions.title: Cognitive
activities: play logic games like puzzles
engage in storytelling and ask predictive questions
explore nature and categorize plants or animals
watchFor: lack of interest in problem-solving activities

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: can retell a story in sequence
activities: read books together and discuss the story
play word games like Scrabble Junior
encourage writing simple sentences or stories
watchFor: limited vocabulary or difficulty expressing thoughts

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: hops, skips, and jumps with ease
activities: play outdoor games like tag or hide and seek
practice art activities like cutting and drawing
encourage sports or physical activities
watchFor: lack of interest in physical play

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: makes friends and engages in cooperative play
activities: arrange playdates with peers
participate in group activities or team sports
engage in role-play scenarios
watchFor: struggles with taking turns or sharing

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: begins to understand the feelings of others
activities: talk about emotions and share feelings
encourage journaling or drawing feelings
role-play different emotional scenarios

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: asks numerous questions about the world
shows interest in how things work
activities: do science experiments together
explore nature walks and collect items
visit museums or educational places
watchFor: lack of questions or interest in the environment
disinterest in exploration or trying new things
answers or engagement that seem superficial

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: can focus on tasks for 10-20 minutes
begins to use varied strategies to learn
can list steps to complete a simple task
activities: set up learning stations with varied activities
encourage participation in games that require turn-taking
provide tasks with clear, achievable goals
watchFor: inability to stay focused on activities

dimensions.title: Independence
milestones: can dress themselves with little assistance
activities: encourage chores appropriate for age
let them choose between options for meals or activities
allow them to manage basic hygiene tasks
watchFor: frequent dependencies on adults for simple tasks
lack of ownership of personal belongings
